_notes: Source of truth for the 1.2 practice set. "linear" exercises: q is a linear equation (var: letter, default x; param: letter k asks for the value that makes it true for every x); the answer is computed by solving it, every line must have the same solution, and each wrong e is the arithmetic of one named mistake. "match" uses check count (One solution / No solution / Infinitely many solutions) and "multi" uses check count:none|one|all. Chips: DIST and COLLECT yellow, COMBINE green, ISOLATE blue. See docs/exercises.md.
title: Variables on Both Sides

exercises.read: Five x plus three equals two x plus fifteen. Solve for x.
say: Both sides have x, so collect the x terms on one side. Subtract two x from both sides. Three x plus three equals fifteen.
Now undo the plus three. Subtract three from both sides: three x equals twelve.
Divide both sides by three. x equals four.

wrong.why: Adding 2x makes 7x + 3 = 15 and x = 12/7, but the 2x on the right has to cancel: subtract it from both sides.
wrong.say: add two x to both sides instead of subtracting it

wrong.why: To undo +3 you subtract 3 from both sides; adding it gives 18 instead of 12.
wrong.say: add three instead of subtracting it

wrong.why: 3x = 12 is not finished: divide both sides by 3 to get x = 4.
wrong.say: forget to divide by three

exercises.read: Nine x minus seven equals four x plus eight. Solve for x.
say: Subtract four x from both sides. Five x minus seven equals eight.
Undo the minus seven by adding seven to both sides: five x equals fifteen.
Divide both sides by five. x equals three.

wrong.why: Adding 4x gives 13x − 7 = 8. The 4x on the right has to cancel, so subtract it: 9x − 4x = 5x.
wrong.say: add four x instead of subtracting it

wrong.why: To undo −7 you add 7: 8 + 7 = 15, not 8 − 7.
wrong.say: subtract seven instead of adding it

wrong.why: After collecting, the coefficient is 5, not 9: you divide by what is left after subtracting 4x.
wrong.say: divide by the original nine instead of five

exercises.prompt: Plan A costs $15 plus $4 per visit. Plan B costs $7 per visit. Solve for v, the number of visits after which they cost the same.
exercises.read: Plan A costs fifteen dollars plus four dollars a visit. Plan B costs seven dollars a visit. After how many visits do they cost the same? Let v be the number of visits, so fifteen plus four v equals seven v.
say: Gather the v terms. Subtract four v from both sides. Fifteen equals three v.
Divide both sides by three. v equals five. At five visits, both plans cost thirty-five dollars.

wrong.why: The v terms are on opposite sides, so you subtract: 7v − 4v = 3v. Adding gives 11v.
wrong.say: add four v instead of subtracting it

wrong.why: To undo 3v you divide by 3. Multiplying turns 15 into 45.
wrong.say: multiply by three instead of dividing

wrong.why: 15 = 3v means v = 15 ÷ 3. Dividing 3 by 15 flips it.
wrong.say: divide three by fifteen

exercises.read: Three x plus twenty equals seven x. Solve for x.
say: The right side has more x, so subtract three x from both sides. Twenty equals four x.
Divide both sides by four. x equals five.

wrong.why: 3x and 7x are on opposite sides: moving 3x over gives 7x − 3x = 4x, not 7x + 3x = 10x.
wrong.say: add the x terms instead of subtracting

wrong.why: The 3x on the left has to go too: 7x − 3x = 4x, so you divide by 4.
wrong.say: ignore the three x and divide by seven

wrong.why: To undo 4x you divide by 4. Multiplying gives 80.
wrong.say: multiply by four instead of dividing

exercises.read: Three times the quantity x plus four equals x plus twenty. Solve for x.
say: Distribute first: three times x is three x, and three times four is twelve. Three x plus twelve equals x plus twenty.
Subtract x from both sides. Two x plus twelve equals twenty.
Subtract twelve from both sides: two x equals eight.
Divide both sides by two. x equals four.

wrong.why: 3(x + 4) is 3x + 12: the 3 multiplies the 4 as well.
wrong.say: forget to multiply the four by three

wrong.why: x is on the right, so subtract it: 3x − x = 2x. Adding gives 4x.
wrong.say: add x to both sides instead of subtracting it

wrong.why: To undo +12 you subtract 12: 20 − 12 = 8, not 20 + 12.
wrong.say: add twelve instead of subtracting it

exercises.read: Two x plus nine equals six x plus twenty-one. Solve for x.
say: Subtract two x from both sides, so the larger x term stays positive. Nine equals four x plus twenty-one.
Subtract twenty-one from both sides. Nine minus twenty-one is negative twelve.
Divide both sides by four. x equals negative three.

wrong.why: 9 − 21 is negative, so −12 ÷ 4 = −3. Keep the sign.
wrong.say: lose the negative sign

wrong.why: To undo +21 you subtract it from 9: 9 − 21, not 9 + 21.
wrong.say: add twenty-one instead of subtracting it

wrong.why: Moving 2x gives 6x − 2x = 4x, not 6x + 2x = 8x.
wrong.say: add the x terms instead of subtracting

exercises.read: Four x plus five equals x plus twelve. Solve for x.
say: Subtract x from both sides. Three x plus five equals twelve.
Subtract five from both sides. Three x equals seven.
Divide both sides by three. x equals seven over three. It is not a whole number, and that is fine.

wrong.why: To undo +5 you subtract it: 12 − 5 = 7, not 12 + 5.
wrong.say: add five instead of subtracting it

wrong.why: Moving x to the left gives 4x − x = 3x, not 4x + x = 5x.
wrong.say: combine four x and x into five x

wrong.why: To undo 3x you divide by 3. Multiplying gives 21.
wrong.say: multiply by three instead of dividing

exercises.prompt: Shop A charges $18 plus $4 per hour to rent a bike. Shop B charges $7 per hour. Solve for h, the number of hours after which they cost the same.
exercises.read: Shop A charges eighteen dollars plus four dollars an hour. Shop B charges seven dollars an hour. After how many hours do they cost the same? Let h be the number of hours, so eighteen plus four h equals seven h.
say: Subtract four h from both sides. Eighteen equals three h.
Divide both sides by three. h equals six. At six hours, both shops charge forty-two dollars.

wrong.why: The h terms are on opposite sides: 7h − 4h = 3h. Adding gives 11h.
wrong.say: add four h instead of subtracting it

wrong.why: To undo 3h you divide by 3; subtracting 3 from 18 doesn't undo it.
wrong.say: subtract three instead of dividing

wrong.why: 18 = 3h means h = 18 ÷ 3, not 3 ÷ 18.
wrong.say: divide three by eighteen

exercises.read: Four times the quantity x minus three equals two times the quantity x plus five. Solve for x.
say: Distribute on both sides. Four x minus twelve equals two x plus ten.
Subtract two x from both sides. Two x minus twelve equals ten.
Add twelve to both sides. Two x equals twenty-two.
Divide both sides by two. x equals eleven.

wrong.why: 4(x − 3) is 4x − 12: the 4 multiplies the 3 as well.
wrong.say: multiply only the x by four and leave the three alone

wrong.why: 2(x + 5) is 2x + 10: the 2 multiplies the 5 as well.
wrong.say: multiply only the x by two and leave the five alone

wrong.why: To undo −12 you add 12: 10 + 12 = 22, not 10 − 12.
wrong.say: subtract twelve instead of adding it

exercises.read: Seven minus three x equals two x minus eight. Solve for x.
say: Add three x to both sides, so the x term ends up positive. Seven equals five x minus eight.
Add eight to both sides. Fifteen equals five x.
Divide both sides by five. x equals three.

wrong.why: To undo −8 you add 8: 7 + 8 = 15, not 7 − 8.
wrong.say: subtract eight instead of adding it

wrong.why: Adding 3x to both sides gives 2x + 3x = 5x, not 2x − 3x.
wrong.say: combine the x terms as two x minus three x

wrong.why: 15 = 5x is not finished: divide both sides by 5.
wrong.say: forget to divide by five

exercises.read: Five x plus two equals nine x plus eleven. Solve for x.
say: Subtract five x from both sides, so the x term stays positive. Two equals four x plus eleven.
Subtract eleven from both sides. Two minus eleven is negative nine.
Divide both sides by four. x equals negative nine over four.

wrong.why: 2 − 11 is negative, so the answer is negative too.
wrong.say: lose the negative sign

wrong.why: To undo +11 you subtract it from 2: 2 − 11, not 11 + 2.
wrong.say: add eleven and two instead of subtracting

wrong.why: Moving 5x gives 9x − 5x = 4x, not 9x + 5x = 14x.
wrong.say: add the x terms instead of subtracting

exercises.read: Three times the quantity x plus two, plus x, equals two x plus twenty. Solve for x.
say: Distribute the three. Three x plus six, plus x, equals two x plus twenty.
Combine like terms on the left: three x plus x is four x. Four x plus six equals two x plus twenty.
Subtract two x from both sides. Two x plus six equals twenty.
Subtract six from both sides. Two x equals fourteen.
Divide both sides by two. x equals seven.

wrong.why: 3(x + 2) is 3x + 6: the 3 multiplies the 2 as well.
wrong.say: multiply the three by x but not by two

wrong.why: Moving 2x gives 4x − 2x = 2x, not 4x + 2x = 6x.
wrong.say: add two x instead of subtracting it

wrong.why: 2x = 14 is not finished: divide both sides by 2.
wrong.say: forget to divide by two

exercises.prompt: Match each equation with the number of solutions it has.
exercises.read: Match each equation with the number of solutions it has. Think about what is left when the x terms cancel.
exercises.say_answer: Two have one solution, two have none, and two have infinitely many. When the x terms cancel, a false statement means no solution and a true one means every number works.

pairs.why: The x terms don't cancel: collecting leaves 4x, so x has one value.
pairs.say: Two x minus seven equals six x plus five. Collecting the x terms leaves four x, so x has exactly one value, negative three. One solution.

pairs.why: The coefficients are different (9 and 5), so the x terms don't cancel.
pairs.say: Nine x minus four equals five x plus eight. Subtract five x: four x minus four equals eight, so four x equals twelve and x equals three. One solution.

pairs.why: Same coefficients, different constants: 8 = −3 is false.
pairs.say: Five x plus eight equals five x minus three. Subtract five x and you get eight equals negative three, which is false. No solution.

pairs.why: The right side is 6x − 8, so 1 = −8 is false.
pairs.say: Six x plus one equals two times the quantity three x minus four. Distribute: six x minus eight. Subtract six x: one equals negative eight, which is false. No solution.

pairs.why: The left side is 3x + 12, the same as the right: 12 = 12 is always true.
pairs.say: Three times the quantity x plus four is three x plus twelve, the same as the right side. Subtract three x: twelve equals twelve, always true. Infinitely many solutions.

pairs.why: The left side simplifies to 2x + 6, the same as the right.
pairs.say: Distribute the negative two: four x minus two x plus six. Combine: two x plus six equals two x plus six. Both sides are the same, so infinitely many solutions.

exercises.prompt: Select all the equations that have no solution.
exercises.read: Which of these equations have no solution? Choose all that apply.
exercises.say_answer: Three equations have no solution: three x plus seven equals three x minus two, four times the quantity x minus one equals four x plus three, and eight x minus three times the quantity x plus one equals five x plus one. In each one the x terms cancel and a false statement is left.

options.say: Three x plus seven equals three x minus two. Subtract three x: seven equals negative two. False, so no solution.

options.why: It simplifies to 2x + 10 = 2x + 10, which is always true: infinitely many solutions.
options.say: Two times the quantity x plus five is two x plus ten, exactly the right side. Always true, so infinitely many solutions, not none.

options.why: The coefficients differ (5 and 4), so there is exactly one solution: x = 0.
options.say: Five x minus one equals four x minus one. The x coefficients are different, five and four, so there is one solution, x equals zero.

options.why: 4(x − 1) = 4x − 4, and −4 is not 3: same coefficients, different constants.
options.say: Distribute: four x minus four equals four x plus three. Subtract four x: negative four equals three. False, so no solution.

options.why: The coefficients differ (1 and 2), so there is one solution: x = 0.
options.say: x plus six equals two x plus six. The coefficients are different, one and two, so there is one solution, x equals zero. Matching constants don't change that.

options.why: The left side is 5x − 3, so 5x − 3 = 5x + 1: same coefficients, different constants.
options.say: Distribute and combine on the left: eight x minus three x minus three is five x minus three. So five x minus three equals five x plus one. The x terms cancel and negative three equals one is false. No solution.

exercises.prompt: For what value of k does this equation have infinitely many solutions?
exercises.read: Three x plus nine equals three x plus k. For what value of k does this equation have infinitely many solutions?
say: For infinitely many solutions, both sides must end up identical. Subtract three x from both sides: nine equals k. So k must be nine, and then both sides are three x plus nine.

wrong.why: Both sides need the same constant: +9 on the left means k = +9, not −9.
wrong.say: flip the sign of nine

wrong.why: The x terms already match (3x on both sides). Only the constants must match: k = 9.
wrong.say: divide the nine by the coefficient three

wrong.why: The 3x terms cancel and are not added to the constant: k = 9.
wrong.say: add the three to the nine

exercises.prompt: Gym A charges $50 to join plus $6 per visit. Gym B charges $10 per visit. Solve for v, the number of visits after which they cost the same.
exercises.read: Gym A charges fifty dollars to join plus six dollars a visit. Gym B charges ten dollars a visit. After how many visits do they cost the same? Let v be the number of visits, so fifty plus six v equals ten v.
say: Subtract six v from both sides. Fifty equals four v.
Divide both sides by four. v equals twenty-five over two, which is twelve and a half. Visits come in whole numbers, so the costs cross between visit twelve and visit thirteen.

wrong.why: The v terms are on opposite sides: 10v − 6v = 4v. Adding gives 16v.
wrong.say: add six v instead of subtracting it

wrong.why: To undo 4v you divide by 4; subtracting 4 from 50 doesn't undo it.
wrong.say: subtract four instead of dividing

wrong.why: 50 = 4v means v = 50 ÷ 4, not 4 ÷ 50.
wrong.say: divide four by fifty
